headline: European Markets Fall as Cost-of-Living Protests Turn Violent in France
summary: European stocks declined, led by losses in Paris and Milan, as violent protests over the cost of living erupted in France and President Macron condemned the unrest.
why: Civil unrest in major European economies can disrupt local commerce, hurt investor confidence, and weigh heavily on domestic banking and luxury sectors.

impacts.name: France
impacts.why: Civil unrest disrupts domestic economic activity and undermines investor confidence in local assets.

why_moved: Widespread social protests and violence create economic uncertainty, prompting investors to pull capital from domestic European equities and pressure the euro.
